headline: Wyoming Joins Elite Group of No-Kill States
meta_description: Wyoming becomes the sixth US state to achieve no-kill status, with every animal shelter saving at least 90% of dogs and cats for 12 consecutive months.
summary_short: Wyoming reaches no-kill status as every shelter in the state saves at least 90% of dogs and cats in its care for a full year.
body:
Wyoming has become the sixth U.S. state to achieve no-kill status, marking a major milestone for animal welfare in the region. The achievement means every animal shelter across Wyoming is now saving at least 90 percent of the dogs and cats in its care.

This distinction reflects a sustained commitment to life-saving practices. Shelters had to maintain their 90 percent save rate for 12 consecutive months to qualify for the state's no-kill designation. The standard applies uniformly across the state, ensuring that no community was left behind in the effort.

Wyoming joins a small but growing group of states that have successfully transformed their shelter systems to prioritize adoptions, foster programs, and medical care over euthanasia. The achievement represents the collective work of shelter staff, volunteers, and animal advocates who refused to accept preventable deaths.
quick_facts: Wyoming is the sixth US state to reach no-kill status
Every shelter must save at least 90% of dogs and cats
Save rate maintained for 12 consecutive months required
